1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Deterministic generator for the YCbCr test-image matrix.
3: 
4: This script produces 17 YCbCr (``PhotometricInterpretation = 6``) TIFF
5: fixtures in ``tests/ycbcr_images/`` and one matching ground-truth P6 PPM
6: per fixture in ``tests/reference_images/``.
7: 
8: The 17-case matrix
9: ------------------
10: * 9 subsampling fixtures (64x48): 1x1, 2x1, 1x2, 2x2, 4x1, 1x4, 4x2,
11:   2x4 and 4x4. These exercise real chroma subsampling written by
12:   ``rgb2ycbcr``; tags and pixel data agree, so they are conversion-verified.
13: * 5 variant fixtures (64x48): ``ycbcr-cosited`` (positioning = 2),
14:   ``ycbcr-custom-coeffs`` (BT.709 coefficients), ``ycbcr-custom-refbw``
15:   (headroom/footroom reference values), ``ycbcr-planar-2x2``
16:   (PlanarConfiguration = 2) and ``ycbcr-tiled-2x2`` (tiled organization).
17:   These are tag-reading-only fixtures: ``tiffset`` changes tag values
18:   without reorganizing the pixel data, so their pixels do not necessarily
19:   match the patched tags. They must not be used for conversion checks.
20: * 3 odd-dimension fixtures: ``ycbcr-odd-2x2`` (61x47),
21:   ``ycbcr-odd-4x4`` (63x61) and ``ycbcr-odd-mixed`` (62x47, 2x1).
22:   Tags and pixel data agree, so these are conversion-verified.
23: 
24: The tiled deviation
25: -------------------
26: ``tiffcp`` refuses subsampled input, so ``ycbcr-tiled-2x2.tif`` is tiled
27: while still 1x1-subsampled; the ``YCbCrSubsampling`` tag is set to ``2 2``
28: only afterwards. ``tiffcp`` also drops the four YCbCr tags and resets
29: PhotometricInterpretation to RGB, so the TIFF tags are restored after
30: tiling. Its pixel data is therefore *not* subsampled: this fixture is a
31: tag-reading test only and is not usable for conversion verification.
32: 
33: Toolchain
34: ---------
35: Only libtiff and netpbm command-line tools are used: ``pnmtotiff``,
36: ``rgb2ycbcr``, ``tiffset``, ``tiffcp``, ``tiff2rgba`` and ``tifftopnm``.
37: Source PPMs are written as binary P6 with the standard library (``bytes``
38: plus ``zlib.crc32`` for the deterministic seed). There is no external
39: imaging-library dependency and no ImageMagick dependency. Ground-truth PPMs
40: come exclusively from ``tiff2rgba`` followed by ``tifftopnm``. libtiff's YCbCr
41: RGBA reader cannot decode 1x4 or 2x4 subsampling, so those two references are
42: rendered from the matching RGB source TIFF through that same pipeline.
43: 
44: Usage (from the repository root)::
45: 
46:     python3 tests/ycbcr_images/generate_ycbcr.py
47: """
48: 
49: import subprocess
50: import zlib
51: from pathlib import Path
52: 
53: BASE_W, BASE_H = 64, 48
54: 
55: IMAGE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
56: REFERENCE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "reference_images"
57: TMP_DIR = Path("/tmp/opencode/ycbcr-gen")
58: 
59: # (name, horizontal subsampling, vertical subsampling) -- all 64x48.
60: SUBSAMPLING_CASES = [
61:     ("ycbcr-1x1", 1, 1),
62:     ("ycbcr-2x1", 2, 1),
63:     ("ycbcr-1x2", 1, 2),
64:     ("ycbcr-2x2", 2, 2),
65:     ("ycbcr-4x1", 4, 1),
66:     ("ycbcr-1x4", 1, 4),
67:     ("ycbcr-4x2", 4, 2),
68:     ("ycbcr-2x4", 2, 4),
69:     ("ycbcr-4x4", 4, 4),
70: ]
71: 
72: # (name, width, height, horizontal subsampling, vertical subsampling).
73: ODD_CASES = [
74:     ("ycbcr-odd-2x2", 61, 47, 2, 2),
75:     ("ycbcr-odd-4x4", 63, 61, 4, 4),
76:     ("ycbcr-odd-mixed", 62, 47, 2, 1),
77: ]
78: 
79: VARIANT_NAMES = [
80:     "ycbcr-cosited",
81:     "ycbcr-custom-coeffs",
82:     "ycbcr-custom-refbw",
83:     "ycbcr-planar-2x2",
84:     "ycbcr-tiled-2x2",
85: ]
86: 
87: ALL_NAMES = (
88:     [name for name, _, _ in SUBSAMPLING_CASES]
89:     + [name for name, _, _, _, _ in ODD_CASES]
90:     + VARIANT_NAMES
91: )
92: 
93: 
94: def run(*args, stdin=None, stdout=None, stderr=None):
95:     """Run an external tool, aborting on a non-zero exit status."""
96:     subprocess.run([str(a) for a in args], check=True,
97:                    stdin=stdin, stdout=stdout, stderr=stderr)
98: 
99: 
100: def write_binary_ppm(path, w, h, pixels):
101:     """Write a binary (P6) Netpbm image with the standard library only."""
102:     with open(path, "wb") as f:
103:         f.write(f"P6\n{w} {h}\n255\n".encode("ascii"))
104:         for row in pixels:
105:             for (r, g, b) in row:
106:                 f.write(bytes((r, g, b)))
107: 
108: 
109: def source_pixels(w, h, seed):
110:     """Deterministic RGB source pattern seeded by ``zlib.crc32``."""
111:     return [
112:         [
113:             (
114:                 (x * 37 + y * 11 + seed * 53) % 256,
115:                 (x * 7 + y * 29 + seed * 17) % 256,
116:                 (x * 13 + y * 5 + seed * 31) % 256,
117:             )
118:             for x in range(w)
119:         ]
120:         for y in range(h)
121:     ]
122: 
123: 
124: def make_rgb_tiff(name, w, h):
125:     """Write a binary P6 source and convert it to an RGB TIFF."""
126:     ppm = TMP_DIR / f"{name}-src.ppm"
127:     tif = TMP_DIR / f"{name}-src.tif"
128:     seed = zlib.crc32(name.encode()) & 0xFFFFFFFF
129:     write_binary_ppm(ppm, w, h, source_pixels(w, h, seed))
130:     with open(ppm, "rb") as fin, open(tif, "wb") as fout:
131:         run("pnmtotiff", stdin=fin, stdout=fout,
132:             stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
133:     return tif
134: 
135: 
136: def make_ycbcr_tiff(name, rgb_tif, w, h, hs, vs, out_tif):
137:     """Encode an RGB TIFF as YCbCr with all four YCbCr tags written."""
138:     run("rgb2ycbcr", "-c", "none", "-h", hs, "-v", vs, "-r", h,
139:         rgb_tif, out_tif, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
140:     return out_tif
141: 
142: 
143: def set_tag(path, tag, *values):
144:     """Set a TIFF tag with tiffset.
145: 
146:     RATIONAL values are passed with no explicit count; supplying one
147:     corrupts the first value.
148:     """
149:     run("tiffset", "-s", tag, *values, path)
150: 
151: 
152: def make_ground_truth(name, tif):
153:     """Produce the P6 PPM ground truth with tiff2rgba + tifftopnm."""
154:     rgba = TMP_DIR / f"{name}-rgba.tif"
155:     ppm = REFERENCE_DIR / f"{name}.ppm"
156:     run("tiff2rgba", "-n", "-c", "none", tif, rgba)
157:     with open(rgba, "rb") as fin, open(ppm, "wb") as fout:
158:         run("tifftopnm", stdin=fin, stdout=fout,
159:             stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
160: 
161: 
162: # libtiff's YCbCr RGBA reader has no 1x4 or 2x4 strip/tile routine, so
163: # tiff2rgba rejects those two YCbCr encodings. Their ground truth is
164: # rendered from the equivalent RGB source TIFF through the very same
165: # tiff2rgba + tifftopnm pipeline; that source is the exact image fed to
166: # rgb2ycbcr, so it is the correct expected RGB result.
167: UNSUPPORTED_FOR_TIFF2RGBA = {(1, 4), (2, 4)}
168: 
169: 
170: def remove_stale_fixtures():
171:     """Remove fixtures that are not part of the current 17-case matrix."""
172:     expected_tifs = {f"{name}.tif" for name in ALL_NAMES}
173:     expected_ppms = {f"{name}.ppm" for name in ALL_NAMES}
174:     for path in IMAGE_DIR.glob("ycbcr-*.tif"):
175:         if path.name not in expected_tifs:
176:             path.unlink()
177:     for path in REFERENCE_DIR.glob("ycbcr-*.ppm"):
178:         if path.name not in expected_ppms:
179:             path.unlink()
180: 
181: 
182: def main():
183:     TMP_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
184:     IMAGE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
185:     REFERENCE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
186:     remove_stale_fixtures()
187: 
188:     # 9 full-resolution subsampling fixtures: conversion-verified.
189:     for name, hs, vs in SUBSAMPLING_CASES:
190:         rgb = make_rgb_tiff(name, BASE_W, BASE_H)
191:         out = IMAGE_DIR / f"{name}.tif"
192:         make_ycbcr_tiff(name, rgb, BASE_W, BASE_H, hs, vs, out)
193:         source = rgb if (hs, vs) in UNSUPPORTED_FOR_TIFF2RGBA else out
194:         make_ground_truth(name, source)
195: 
196:     # 3 odd-dimension fixtures: conversion-verified.
197:     for name, w, h, hs, vs in ODD_CASES:
198:         rgb = make_rgb_tiff(name, w, h)
199:         out = IMAGE_DIR / f"{name}.tif"
200:         make_ycbcr_tiff(name, rgb, w, h, hs, vs, out)
201:         make_ground_truth(name, out)
202: 
203:     # 5 variants: tag-reading only (see module docstring).
204:     # cosited -- patch positioning on a 2x2 base.
205:     name = "ycbcr-cosited"
206:     rgb = make_rgb_tiff(name, BASE_W, BASE_H)
207:     out = IMAGE_DIR / f"{name}.tif"
208:     make_ycbcr_tiff(name, rgb, BASE_W, BASE_H, 2, 2, out)
209:     set_tag(out, "YCbCrPositioning", 2)
210:     make_ground_truth(name, out)
211: 
212:     # custom coefficients -- patch tag 529 on a 1x1 base.
213:     name = "ycbcr-custom-coeffs"
214:     rgb = make_rgb_tiff(name, BASE_W, BASE_H)
215:     out = IMAGE_DIR / f"{name}.tif"
216:     make_ycbcr_tiff(name, rgb, BASE_W, BASE_H, 1, 1, out)
217:     set_tag(out, "YCbCrCoefficients", 0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722)
218:     make_ground_truth(name, out)
219: 
220:     # custom reference black/white -- patch tag 532 on a 1x1 base.
221:     name = "ycbcr-custom-refbw"
222:     rgb = make_rgb_tiff(name, BASE_W, BASE_H)
223:     out = IMAGE_DIR / f"{name}.tif"
224:     make_ycbcr_tiff(name, rgb, BASE_W, BASE_H, 1, 1, out)
225:     set_tag(out, "ReferenceBlackWhite", 15, 235, 128, 240, 128, 240)
226:     make_ground_truth(name, out)
227: 
228:     # separate planar configuration -- patch tag 284 without moving pixels.
229:     # The ground truth is rendered from the chunky TIFF before the patch.
230:     name = "ycbcr-planar-2x2"
231:     rgb = make_rgb_tiff(name, BASE_W, BASE_H)
232:     out = IMAGE_DIR / f"{name}.tif"
233:     make_ycbcr_tiff(name, rgb, BASE_W, BASE_H, 2, 2, out)
234:     make_ground_truth(name, out)
235:     set_tag(out, "PlanarConfiguration", 2)
236: 
237:     # tiled -- tiffcp refuses subsampled input and drops the YCbCr tags.
238:     # Tile a 1x1 image, restore PI=6 and all four tags, then patch 530.
239:     # The ground truth is rendered from the 1x1 stripped TIFF before tiling.
240:     name = "ycbcr-tiled-2x2"
241:     rgb = make_rgb_tiff(name, BASE_W, BASE_H)
242:     stripped = TMP_DIR / f"{name}-1x1.tif"
243:     out = IMAGE_DIR / f"{name}.tif"
244:     make_ycbcr_tiff(name, rgb, BASE_W, BASE_H, 1, 1, stripped)
245:     make_ground_truth(name, stripped)
246:     run("tiffcp", "-t", "-w", "16", "-l", "16", "-c", "none",

249:     set_tag(out, "YCbCrCoefficients", 0.299, 0.587, 0.114)

1: # YCbCr (PhotometricInterpretation = 6) Support Reference
2: 
3: This document describes YCbCr (`PhotometricInterpretation = 6`) images as
4: defined by Section 21 of the TIFF 6.0 specification.
5: 
6: ## Scope
7: 
8: - YCbCr image encoding as defined by TIFF 6.0 Section 21.
9: - Conversion between RGB and YCbCr.
10: - Chroma subsampling, positioning, and reference black/white handling.
11: - Minimum requirements for a valid YCbCr TIFF.
12: - Mapping of the test images in `tests/ycbcr_images/` to the specification
13:   topics they exercise.
14: 
15: ## Tag definitions
16: 
17: The following TIFF tags describe the color information of an image whose
18: `PhotometricInterpretation = 6` (YCbCr). They are defined in TIFF 6.0
19: Section 21.
20: 
21: | Tag | Name | TIFF value | Type | Count | Default | Description |
22: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
23: | 529 | YCbCrCoefficients | 0x0211 | RATIONAL (5) / SRATIONAL (10) | 3 | ITU-R BT.601 luma coefficients | Coefficients used for the transformation from RGB to YCbCr. |
24: | 530 | YCbCrSubsampling | 0x0212 | SHORT (3) | 2 | 2, 2 | Horizontal and vertical subsampling factors of the chroma components. |
25: | 531 | YCbCrPositioning | 0x0213 | SHORT (3) | 1 | 1 | Positioning of the chroma samples relative to the luminance samples. |
26: | 532 | ReferenceBlackWhite | 0x0214 | RATIONAL (5) | 6 | (0, 255, 128, 255, 128, 255) | Reference black and white data values (headroom/footroom) per component. |
27: 
28: Notes on the individual tags:
29: 
30: - **YCbCrCoefficients (529 / 0x0211):** Type RATIONAL (TIFF data type 5) or
31:   SRATIONAL (TIFF data type 10), with **3 values** (the RGB -> YCbCr
32:   transformation coefficients, e.g. the luma row). Defaults to the ITU-R BT.601
33:   coefficients (approximately 0.299, 0.587, 0.114 for the red, green and blue
34:   contributions to luma).
35: - **YCbCrSubsampling (530 / 0x0212):** Type SHORT (TIFF data type 3), **2
36:   values** — the horizontal subsampling factor and the vertical subsampling
37:   factor. Default is **2, 2** (chroma subsampled by 2 on both axes). Legal
38:   factors are **1, 2 and 4**
39:   (1 = no subsampling, 2 = half resolution, 4 = quarter resolution along the
40:   axis).
41: - **YCbCrPositioning (531 / 0x0213):** Type SHORT (TIFF data type 3), **1
42:   value**. Default is **1 = centered**. The alternative value is **2 = co-sited**
43:   (chroma sample points aligned with luma sample positions, as used e.g. in
44:   broadcast 4:2:2 workflows).
45: - **ReferenceBlackWhite (532 / 0x0214):** Type RATIONAL (TIFF data type 5), **6
46:   values**. The values are grouped in pairs of (reference black, reference
47:   white) per pixel component, ordered like the components of the
48:   `PhotometricInterpretation = 6` image (Y, Cb, Cr). Default value set:
49:   Y black/white = 0/255, Cb black/white = 128/255, Cr black/white = 128/255.
50: 
51: ## Conversion formulas
52: 
53: ### Forward conversion (RGB -> YCbCr), ITU-R BT.601
54: 
55: - `Y  = 0.299 * R + 0.587 * G + 0.114 * B`
56: - `Cb = -0.168736 * R - 0.331264 * G + 0.5 * B + 128`
57: - `Cr = 0.5 * R - 0.418688 * G - 0.081312 * B + 128`
58: 
59: ### Reverse conversion (YCbCr -> RGB), ITU-R BT.601
60: 
61: - `R = Y + 1.402 * (Cr - 128)`
62: - `G = Y - 0.344136 * (Cb - 128) - 0.714136 * (Cr - 128)`
63: - `B = Y + 1.772 * (Cb - 128)`
64: 
65: ### Reference black/white / headroom and footroom
66: 
67: The `ReferenceBlackWhite` tag supplies, per component, a reference black value
68: and a reference white value. These define the headroom/footroom range of the
69: image data: the black value corresponds to the black end of the coding range and
70: the white value to the white end. The values stored in the image are **codes**;
71: `ReferenceBlackWhite` defines how those codes scale into full-range values when
72: converting to RGB.
73: 
74: For each component the forward scaling is:
75: 
76: `FullRangeValue = (code - ReferenceBlack) * CodingRange / (ReferenceWhite - ReferenceBlack)`
77: 
78: and the reverse scaling is:
79: 
80: `code = (FullRangeValue * (ReferenceWhite - ReferenceBlack) / CodingRange) + ReferenceBlack`
81: 
82: `CodingRange` is the range of full-range values: `2^BitsPerSample - 1` for Y and
83: RGB (255 for 8-bit samples), but **127 for Cb and Cr**. That difference matters:
84: with the default reference values Cb/Cr run from code 128 to code 255, so the
85: chroma scaling reduces to `(code - 128) * 127 / (255 - 128) = code - 128`. This
86: is why the no-headroom case amounts to simply subtracting 128, and why the `128`
87: in `R = Y + 1.402 * (Cr - 128)` is the `ReferenceBlack` value for Cb/Cr in the
88: no-headroom case, not a magic number.
89: 
90: For YCbCr the default reference values are black = 0 and white = 255 for the
91: luma component (Y), and black = 128 and white = 255 for the chroma components
92: (Cb/Cr). Merely subtracting 128 is correct only for these defaults. Images with
93: headroom/footroom carry other reference values: for example, with
94: `ReferenceBlackWhite = [15, 235, 128, 240, 128, 240]` a luma code of 235 maps to
95: `255` and a luma code of 15 maps to `0`, using
96: `(code - 15) * 255 / (235 - 15)`. The chroma white reference is 240 rather than
97: the default 255, so subtracting 128 alone leaves chroma under-scaled. Readers
98: must apply the tag's scaling instead of assuming the defaults.
99: 
100: The TIFF 6.0 specification says the default `ReferenceBlackWhite` values are
101: inappropriate for Class Y images and that the tag must be supplied explicitly.
102: In practice many images omit it, so readers must fall back to the YCbCr-specific
103: defaults above (Y 0/255, Cb/Cr 128/255).
104: 
105: ## Subsampling
106: 
107: - The `YCbCrSubsampling` factors describe how the chroma components are
108:   subsampled relative to the luma component.
109: - Legal subsampling factors are **1, 2 and 4**.
110: - The chroma image dimensions are computed by rounding **up** (ceiling) the
111:   luma dimensions divided by the subsampling factor, so that no chroma sample is
112:   dropped for images whose dimensions are not evenly divisible.
113: - For images using subsampling, strip organization (`RowsPerStrip`) must be
114:   consistent with the luma/chroma grid; `RowsPerStrip` is expressed in luma
115:   rows.
116: 
117: ## Positioning
118: 
119: - `YCbCrPositioning = 1` (default): **centered** positioning of the chroma
120:   samples with respect to the luminance samples.
121: - `YCbCrPositioning = 2`: **co-sited** positioning (chroma sample points aligned
122:   with luma sample points, e.g. recommended for 4:2:2 workflows).
123: 
124: ## Minimum requirements for YCbCr images
125: 
126: In addition to the general Baseline TIFF requirements, a YCbCr file must have:
127: 
128: - `SamplesPerPixel = 3` (Y, Cb, Cr).
129: - `BitsPerSample = 8, 8, 8`.
130: - `Compression = 1` (none), `5` (LZW) or `7` (JPEG; TIFF Technical Note 2).
131: - `PhotometricInterpretation = 6` (YCbCr).
132: - `PlanarConfig = 1` (chunky) or `2` (separate).
133: - `ReferenceBlackWhite`: required by the TIFF 6.0 specification. Readers must
134:   nevertheless handle its absence by falling back to the YCbCr-specific
135:   defaults above (Y 0/255, Cb/Cr 128/255), because many real-world files omit
136:   tag 532.
137: 
138: ## Generating the test images
139: 
140: `tests/ycbcr_images/generate_ycbcr.py` recreates the fixture set. It requires
141: Python 3 and the libtiff and netpbm command-line tools (`pnmtotiff`,
142: `rgb2ycbcr`, `tiffset`, `tiffcp`, `tiff2rgba`, `tifftopnm`). From the repository
143: root, run:
144: 
145: ```sh
146: python3 tests/ycbcr_images/generate_ycbcr.py
147: ```
148: 
149: The pipeline for each fixture is:
150: 
151: 1. Write a deterministic binary P6 source PPM in pure Python (standard-library
152:    `bytes` and `zlib.crc32`; no external imaging library).
153: 2. `pnmtotiff < src.ppm > src.tif` creates an RGB TIFF.
154: 3. `rgb2ycbcr -c none -h H -v V -r HEIGHT src.tif out.tif` writes the YCbCr
155:    image. This writes all four YCbCr tags (529, 530, 531, 532) with the BT.601
156:    coefficients, centered positioning and default reference values.
157: 4. Attributes that `rgb2ycbcr` cannot produce directly are applied with
158:    `tiffset`. RATIONAL tags are set without a count, e.g.
159:    `tiffset -s YCbCrCoefficients 0.2126 0.7152 0.0722 file`. Tiled organization
160:    uses `tiffcp -t -w 16 -l 16 -c none`; because `tiffcp` refuses subsampled
161:    input it tiles a 1x1 image and the four YCbCr tags plus
162:    `PhotometricInterpretation` are restored afterwards.
163: 5. `tiff2rgba -n -c none <tif> <rgba.tif>` followed by
164:    `tifftopnm <rgba.tif> > ycbcr-*.ppm` produces each ground-truth P6 PPM.
165: 
166: The 17 fixtures are described in the matrix below. Five of them (the variants)
167: are tag-reading tests only: `tiffset` changes tag values without reorganizing
168: pixel data. The tiled fixture is additionally limited in that its pixel data is
169: **not** subsampled — the `YCbCrSubsampling` tag is set to `2 2` after tiling —
170: so it is not usable for conversion verification.
171: 
172: ## ImageMagick limitations
173: 
174: ImageMagick is a general-purpose image converter, but its TIFF writer has a
175: fixed set of capabilities that matter for YCbCr coverage:
176: 
177: - It does **not** write `YCbCrCoefficients` (529), `YCbCrSubsampling` (530),
178:   `YCbCrPositioning` (531), or `ReferenceBlackWhite` (532). Requests through
179:   `-define` or `-sampling-factor` do not create those tags; subsampling through
180:   image resizing changes the pixel dimensions instead of writing the tag.
181: - It does **not** support separate planar configuration
182:   (`PlanarConfiguration = 2`).
183: - It can write only basic YCbCr TIFFs: `PhotometricInterpretation = 6`,
184:   `SamplesPerPixel = 3`, 8-bit samples, uncompressed data, and default or absent
185:   YCbCr tags. Tiling is available through
186:   `-define tiff:tile-geometry=<value>`.
187: 
188: These limits are why the fixtures in this repository are generated with
189: libtiff's `rgb2ycbcr` rather than ImageMagick.
190: 
191: ## Test image matrix
192: 
193: All files are in `tests/ycbcr_images/`. The "Kind" column marks a fixture as a
194: **conversion** test (tags and pixel data agree) or a **tag-reading** test.
195: 
196: ### Subsampling fixtures
197: 
198: Nine 64x48 images with default BT.601 coefficients, centered positioning,
199: default reference values, 8-bit contiguous planes and no compression. Each
200: carries a real `YCbCrSubsampling` value written by `rgb2ycbcr`.
201: 
202: | Test image | Subsampling | Kind | Validates |
203: |---|---|---|---|
204: | `ycbcr-1x1.tif` | 1x1 | conversion | Full-resolution YCbCr with all four tags at their defaults; stripped organization. |
205: | `ycbcr-2x1.tif` | 2x1 | conversion | Horizontal-only chroma subsampling. |
206: | `ycbcr-1x2.tif` | 1x2 | conversion | Vertical-only chroma subsampling. |
207: | `ycbcr-2x2.tif` | 2x2 | conversion | Half-resolution chroma on both axes. |
208: | `ycbcr-4x1.tif` | 4x1 | conversion | Quarter-resolution horizontal chroma. |
209: | `ycbcr-1x4.tif` | 1x4 | conversion | Quarter-resolution vertical chroma. |
210: | `ycbcr-4x2.tif` | 4x2 | conversion | Mixed 4x2 chroma grid. |
211: | `ycbcr-2x4.tif` | 2x4 | conversion | Mixed 2x4 chroma grid. |
212: | `ycbcr-4x4.tif` | 4x4 | conversion | Quarter-resolution chroma on both axes. |
213: 
214: ### Variant fixtures
215: 
216: Five 64x48 images with one non-default attribute each. These are tag-reading
217: tests: `tiffset` changes the tag without reorganizing pixel data.
218: 
219: | Test image | Attribute | Kind | Validates |
220: |---|---|---|---|
221: | `ycbcr-cosited.tif` | Positioning = 2 (co-sited) on a 2x2 base | tag-reading | Co-sited chroma positioning. |
222: | `ycbcr-custom-coeffs.tif` | Coefficients = 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722 on a 1x1 base | tag-reading | Non-default luma coefficients (tag 529). |
223: | `ycbcr-custom-refbw.tif` | RefBW = 15/235/128/240/128/240 on a 1x1 base | tag-reading | Headroom/footroom reference values (tag 532). |
224: | `ycbcr-planar-2x2.tif` | PlanarConfig = 2 on a 2x2 base | tag-reading | Separate-plane configuration (tag 284). |
225: | `ycbcr-tiled-2x2.tif` | 16x16 tiles, 4x3 grid (12 tiles) | tag-reading | Tile tag path together with all four YCbCr tags. |
226: 
227: `ycbcr-tiled-2x2.tif` is a special case: `tiffcp` cannot tile subsampled input,
228: so the image was tiled while still 1x1 and the `YCbCrSubsampling` tag was set to
229: `2 2` afterwards. Its pixel data is therefore not subsampled; the fixture
230: exercises tag reading and tile traversal only.
231: 
232: ### Odd-dimension fixtures
233: 
234: Three images whose width and height are not multiples of the subsampling
235: factors, so the chroma dimensions use the ceiling rule. Tags and pixel data
236: agree, so all three are conversion tests.
237: 
238: | Test image | Dimensions | Subsampling | Kind | Validates |
239: |---|---|---|---|---|
240: | `ycbcr-odd-2x2.tif` | 61x47 | 2x2 | conversion | Ceiling of odd luma dimensions for 2x2 chroma. |
241: | `ycbcr-odd-4x4.tif` | 63x61 | 4x4 | conversion | Ceiling of odd luma dimensions for 4x4 chroma. |
242: | `ycbcr-odd-mixed.tif` | 62x47 | 2x1 | conversion | Ceiling on one axis only for mixed subsampling. |
243: 
244: ## Ground-truth reference images
245: 
246: `tests/reference_images/ycbcr-*.ppm` holds the RGB ground-truth images
247: corresponding to the 17 YCbCr test images, in binary Netpbm PPM (P6) format.
248: Each is produced with `tiff2rgba` followed by `tifftopnm`, and each P6 header
249: matches the dimensions of its TIFF (64x48, or the odd dimensions 61x47, 63x61
250: and 62x47). libtiff's YCbCr RGBA reader cannot decode 1x4 and 2x4 subsampling,
251: so those two references are rendered from the matching RGB source TIFF through
252: the same `tiff2rgba` + `tifftopnm` pipeline.

1: # YCbCr (PhotometricInterpretation = 6) Support Reference
2: 
3: This document describes YCbCr (`PhotometricInterpretation = 6`) images as
4: defined by Section 21 of the TIFF 6.0 specification.
5: 
6: ## Scope
7: 
8: - YCbCr image encoding as defined by TIFF 6.0 Section 21.
9: - Conversion between RGB and YCbCr.
10: - Chroma subsampling, positioning, and reference black/white handling.
11: - Minimum requirements for a valid YCbCr TIFF.
12: - Mapping of the test images in `tests/ycbcr_images/` to the specification
13:   topics they exercise.
14: 
15: ## Tag definitions
16: 
17: The following TIFF tags describe the color information of an image whose
18: `PhotometricInterpretation = 6` (YCbCr). They are defined in TIFF 6.0
19: Section 21.
20: 
21: | Tag | Name | TIFF value | Type | Count | Default | Description |
22: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
23: | 529 | YCbCrCoefficients | 0x0211 | RATIONAL (5) / SRATIONAL (10) | 3 | ITU-R BT.601 luma coefficients | Coefficients used for the transformation from RGB to YCbCr. |
24: | 530 | YCbCrSubsampling | 0x0212 | SHORT (3) | 2 | 2, 2 | Horizontal and vertical subsampling factors of the chroma components. |
25: | 531 | YCbCrPositioning | 0x0213 | SHORT (3) | 1 | 1 | Positioning of the chroma samples relative to the luminance samples. |
26: | 532 | ReferenceBlackWhite | 0x0214 | RATIONAL (5) | 6 | (0, 255, 128, 255, 128, 255) | Reference black and white data values (headroom/footroom) per component. |
27: 
28: Notes on the individual tags:
29: 
30: - **YCbCrCoefficients (529 / 0x0211):** Type RATIONAL (TIFF data type 5) or
31:   SRATIONAL (TIFF data type 10), with **3 values** (the RGB -> YCbCr
32:   transformation coefficients, e.g. the luma row). Defaults to the ITU-R BT.601
33:   coefficients (approximately 0.299, 0.587, 0.114 for the red, green and blue
34:   contributions to luma).
35: - **YCbCrSubsampling (530 / 0x0212):** Type SHORT (TIFF data type 3), **2
36:   values** — the horizontal subsampling factor and the vertical subsampling
37:   factor. Default is **2, 2** (chroma subsampled by 2 on both axes). Legal
38:   factors are **1, 2 and 4**
39:   (1 = no subsampling, 2 = half resolution, 4 = quarter resolution along the
40:   axis).
41: - **YCbCrPositioning (531 / 0x0213):** Type SHORT (TIFF data type 3), **1
42:   value**. Default is **1 = centered**. The alternative value is **2 = co-sited**
43:   (chroma sample points aligned with luma sample positions, as used e.g. in
44:   broadcast 4:2:2 workflows).
45: - **ReferenceBlackWhite (532 / 0x0214):** Type RATIONAL (TIFF data type 5), **6
46:   values**. The values are grouped in pairs of (reference black, reference
47:   white) per pixel component, ordered like the components of the
48:   `PhotometricInterpretation = 6` image (Y, Cb, Cr). Default value set:
49:   Y black/white = 0/255, Cb black/white = 128/255, Cr black/white = 128/255.
50: 
51: ## Conversion formulas
52: 
53: ### Forward conversion (RGB -> YCbCr), ITU-R BT.601
54: 
55: - `Y  = 0.299 * R + 0.587 * G + 0.114 * B`
56: - `Cb = -0.168736 * R - 0.331264 * G + 0.5 * B + 128`
57: - `Cr = 0.5 * R - 0.418688 * G - 0.081312 * B + 128`
58: 
59: ### Reverse conversion (YCbCr -> RGB), ITU-R BT.601
60: 
61: - `R = Y + 1.402 * (Cr - 128)`
62: - `G = Y - 0.344136 * (Cb - 128) - 0.714136 * (Cr - 128)`
63: - `B = Y + 1.772 * (Cb - 128)`
64: 
65: ### Reference black/white / headroom and footroom
66: 
67: The `ReferenceBlackWhite` tag supplies, per component, a reference black value
68: and a reference white value. These define the headroom/footroom range of the
69: image data: the black value corresponds to the black end of the coding range and
70: the white value to the white end. The values stored in the image are **codes**;
71: `ReferenceBlackWhite` defines how those codes scale into full-range values when
72: converting to RGB.
73: 
74: For each component the forward scaling is:
75: 
76: `FullRangeValue = (code - ReferenceBlack) * CodingRange / (ReferenceWhite - ReferenceBlack)`
77: 
78: and the reverse scaling is:
79: 
80: `code = (FullRangeValue * (ReferenceWhite - ReferenceBlack) / CodingRange) + ReferenceBlack`
81: 
82: `CodingRange` is the range of full-range values: `2^BitsPerSample - 1` for Y and
83: RGB (255 for 8-bit samples), but **127 for Cb and Cr**. That difference matters:
84: with the default reference values Cb/Cr run from code 128 to code 255, so the
85: chroma scaling reduces to `(code - 128) * 127 / (255 - 128) = code - 128`. This
86: is why the no-headroom case amounts to simply subtracting 128, and why the `128`
87: in `R = Y + 1.402 * (Cr - 128)` is the `ReferenceBlack` value for Cb/Cr in the
88: no-headroom case, not a magic number.
89: 
90: For YCbCr the default reference values are black = 0 and white = 255 for the
91: luma component (Y), and black = 128 and white = 255 for the chroma components
92: (Cb/Cr). Merely subtracting 128 is correct only for these defaults. Images with
93: headroom/footroom carry other reference values: for example, with
94: `ReferenceBlackWhite = [15, 235, 128, 240, 128, 240]` a luma code of 235 maps to
95: `255` and a luma code of 15 maps to `0`, using
96: `(code - 15) * 255 / (235 - 15)`. The chroma white reference is 240 rather than
97: the default 255, so subtracting 128 alone leaves chroma under-scaled. Readers
98: must apply the tag's scaling instead of assuming the defaults.
99: 
100: The TIFF 6.0 specification says the default `ReferenceBlackWhite` values are
101: inappropriate for Class Y images and that the tag must be supplied explicitly.
102: In practice many images omit it, so readers must fall back to the YCbCr-specific
103: defaults above (Y 0/255, Cb/Cr 128/255).
104: 
105: ## Subsampling
106: 
107: - The `YCbCrSubsampling` factors describe how the chroma components are
108:   subsampled relative to the luma component.
109: - Legal subsampling factors are **1, 2 and 4**.
110: - The chroma image dimensions are computed by rounding **up** (ceiling) the
111:   luma dimensions divided by the subsampling factor, so that no chroma sample is
112:   dropped for images whose dimensions are not evenly divisible.
113: - For images using subsampling, strip organization (`RowsPerStrip`) must be
114:   consistent with the luma/chroma grid; `RowsPerStrip` is expressed in luma
115:   rows.
116: 
117: ## Positioning
118: 
119: - `YCbCrPositioning = 1` (default): **centered** positioning of the chroma
120:   samples with respect to the luminance samples.
121: - `YCbCrPositioning = 2`: **co-sited** positioning (chroma sample points aligned
122:   with luma sample points, e.g. recommended for 4:2:2 workflows).
123: 
124: ## Minimum requirements for YCbCr images
125: 
126: In addition to the general Baseline TIFF requirements, a YCbCr file must have:
127: 
128: - `SamplesPerPixel = 3` (Y, Cb, Cr).
129: - `BitsPerSample = 8, 8, 8`.
130: - `Compression = 1` (none), `5` (LZW) or `7` (JPEG; TIFF Technical Note 2).
131: - `PhotometricInterpretation = 6` (YCbCr).
132: - `PlanarConfig = 1` (chunky) or `2` (separate).
133: - `ReferenceBlackWhite`: required by the TIFF 6.0 specification. Readers must
134:   nevertheless handle its absence by falling back to the YCbCr-specific
135:   defaults above (Y 0/255, Cb/Cr 128/255), because many real-world files omit
136:   tag 532.
137: 
138: ## Generating the test images
139: 
140: `tests/ycbcr_images/generate_ycbcr.py` recreates the fixture set. It requires
141: Python 3 and the libtiff and netpbm command-line tools (`pnmtotiff`,
142: `rgb2ycbcr`, `tiffset`, `tiffcp`, `tiff2rgba`, `tifftopnm`). From the repository
143: root, run:
144: 
145: ```sh
146: python3 tests/ycbcr_images/generate_ycbcr.py
147: ```
148: 
149: The pipeline for each fixture is:
150: 
151: 1. Write a deterministic binary P6 source PPM in pure Python (standard-library
152:    `bytes` and `zlib.crc32`; no external imaging library).
153: 2. `pnmtotiff < src.ppm > src.tif` creates an RGB TIFF.
154: 3. `rgb2ycbcr -c none -h H -v V -r HEIGHT src.tif out.tif` writes the YCbCr
155:    image. This writes all four YCbCr tags (529, 530, 531, 532) with the BT.601
156:    coefficients, centered positioning and default reference values.
157: 4. Attributes that `rgb2ycbcr` cannot produce directly are applied with
158:    `tiffset`. RATIONAL tags are set without a count, e.g.
159:    `tiffset -s YCbCrCoefficients 0.2126 0.7152 0.0722 file`. Tiled organization
160:    uses `tiffcp -t -w 16 -l 16 -c none`; because `tiffcp` refuses subsampled
161:    input it tiles a 1x1 image and the four YCbCr tags plus
162:    `PhotometricInterpretation` are restored afterwards.
163: 5. `tiff2rgba -n -c none <tif> <rgba.tif>` followed by
164:    `tifftopnm <rgba.tif> > ycbcr-*.ppm` produces each ground-truth P6 PPM.
165: 
166: The 17 fixtures are described in the matrix below. Five of them (the variants)
167: are tag-reading tests only: `tiffset` changes tag values without reorganizing
168: pixel data. The tiled fixture is additionally limited in that its pixel data is
169: **not** subsampled — the `YCbCrSubsampling` tag is set to `2 2` after tiling —
170: so it is not usable for conversion verification.
171: 
172: ## ImageMagick limitations
173: 
174: ImageMagick is a general-purpose image converter, but its TIFF writer has a
175: fixed set of capabilities that matter for YCbCr coverage:
176: 
177: - It does **not** write `YCbCrCoefficients` (529), `YCbCrSubsampling` (530),
178:   `YCbCrPositioning` (531), or `ReferenceBlackWhite` (532). Requests through
179:   `-define` or `-sampling-factor` do not create those tags; subsampling through
180:   image resizing changes the pixel dimensions instead of writing the tag.
181: - It does **not** support separate planar configuration
182:   (`PlanarConfiguration = 2`).
183: - It can write only basic YCbCr TIFFs: `PhotometricInterpretation = 6`,
184:   `SamplesPerPixel = 3`, 8-bit samples, uncompressed data, and default or absent
185:   YCbCr tags. Tiling is available through
186:   `-define tiff:tile-geometry=<value>`.
187: 
188: These limits are why the fixtures in this repository are generated with
189: libtiff's `rgb2ycbcr` rather than ImageMagick.
190: 
191: ## Test image matrix
192: 
193: All files are in `tests/ycbcr_images/`. The "Kind" column marks a fixture as a
194: **conversion** test (tags and pixel data agree) or a **tag-reading** test.
195: 
196: ### Subsampling fixtures
197:

201: 
202: | Test image | Subsampling | Kind | Validates |
203: |---|---|---|---|
204: | `ycbcr-1x1.tif` | 1x1 | conversion | Full-resolution YCbCr with all four tags at their defaults; stripped organization. |
205: | `ycbcr-2x1.tif` | 2x1 | conversion | Horizontal-only chroma subsampling. |
206: | `ycbcr-1x2.tif` | 1x2 | conversion | Vertical-only chroma subsampling. |

208: | `ycbcr-4x1.tif` | 4x1 | conversion | Quarter-resolution horizontal chroma. |
209: | `ycbcr-1x4.tif` | 1x4 | conversion | Quarter-resolution vertical chroma. |
210: | `ycbcr-4x2.tif` | 4x2 | conversion | Mixed 4x2 chroma grid. |
211: | `ycbcr-2x4.tif` | 2x4 | conversion | Mixed 2x4 chroma grid. |
212: | `ycbcr-4x4.tif` | 4x4 | conversion | Quarter-resolution chroma on both axes. |
213: 
214: ### Variant fixtures
215: 
216: Five 64x48 images with one non-default attribute each. These are tag-reading
217: tests: `tiffset` changes the tag without reorganizing pixel data.
218: 
219: | Test image | Attribute | Kind | Validates |
220: |---|---|---|---|
221: | `ycbcr-cosited.tif` | Positioning = 2 (co-sited) on a 2x2 base | tag-reading | Co-sited chroma positioning. |
222: | `ycbcr-custom-coeffs.tif` | Coefficients = 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722 on a 1x1 base | tag-reading | Non-default luma coefficients (tag 529). |

244: ## Ground-truth reference images
245: 
246: `tests/reference_images/ycbcr-*.ppm` holds the RGB ground-truth images

`ycbcr-odd-mixed` 62x47 (2,1).

Toolchain facts applied (verified in this environment):
- RATIONAL tags are set **without a count**; a count corrupts the first value.
- `tiffcp` refuses subsampled input and drops all four YCbCr tags and resets
  `PhotometricInterpretation` to RGB. Tiled recipe:
  `rgb2ycbcr -c none -h 1 -v 1 -r 48` →
  `tiffcp -t -w 16 -l 16 -c none` →
  `tiffset -s PhotometricInterpretation 6` →
  `tiffset -s YCbCrCoefficients 0.299 0.587 0.114` →
  `tiffset -s YCbCrPositioning 1` →
  `tiffset -s ReferenceBlackWhite 0 255 128 255 128 255` →
  `tiffset -s YCbCrSubsampling 2 2` (libtiff's field name uses lowercase `s`).
  Result: TileWidth/Length=16, 12 tiles; pixel data is **not** subsampled (the
  `2 2` tag is patched on), so this fixture is tag-reading only — documented in
  both the doc and the generator.
- libtiff's YCbCr RGBA reader cannot decode 1x4 or 2x4 subsampling
  (`tiff2rgba` → "Sorry, can not handle image"). Those two PPMs are rendered from
  the *same RGB source TIFF* fed to `rgb2ycbcr`, through the identical
  `tiff2rgba` + `tifftopnm` pipeline; documented in the doc and generator.

1: # YCbCr (PhotometricInterpretation = 6) Support Reference
2: 
3: This document describes YCbCr (`PhotometricInterpretation = 6`) images as
4: defined by Section 21 of the TIFF 6.0 specification.
5: 
6: ## Scope
7: 
8: - YCbCr image encoding as defined by TIFF 6.0 Section 21.
9: - Conversion between RGB and YCbCr.
10: - Chroma subsampling, positioning, and reference black/white handling.
11: - Minimum requirements for a valid YCbCr TIFF.
12: - Mapping of the test images in `tests/ycbcr_images/` to the specification
13:   topics they exercise.
14: 
15: ## Tag definitions
16: 
17: The following TIFF tags describe the color information of an image whose
18: `PhotometricInterpretation = 6` (YCbCr). They are defined in TIFF 6.0
19: Section 21.
20: 
21: | Tag | Name | TIFF value | Type | Count | Default | Description |
22: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
23: | 529 | YCbCrCoefficients | 0x0211 | RATIONAL (5) / SRATIONAL (10) | 3 | ITU-R BT.601 luma coefficients | Coefficients used for the transformation from RGB to YCbCr. |
24: | 530 | YCbCrSubsampling | 0x0212 | SHORT (3) | 2 | 2, 2 | Horizontal and vertical subsampling factors of the chroma components. |
25: | 531 | YCbCrPositioning | 0x0213 | SHORT (3) | 1 | 1 | Positioning of the chroma samples relative to the luminance samples. |
26: | 532 | ReferenceBlackWhite | 0x0214 | RATIONAL (5) | 6 | (0, 255, 128, 255, 128, 255) | Reference black and white data values (headroom/footroom) per component. |
27: 
28: Notes on the individual tags:
29: 
30: - **YCbCrCoefficients (529 / 0x0211):** Type RATIONAL (TIFF data type 5) or
31:   SRATIONAL (TIFF data type 10), with **3 values** (the RGB -> YCbCr
32:   transformation coefficients, e.g. the luma row). Defaults to the ITU-R BT.601
33:   coefficients (approximately 0.299, 0.587, 0.114 for the red, green and blue
34:   contributions to luma).
35: - **YCbCrSubsampling (530 / 0x0212):** Type SHORT (TIFF data type 3), **2
36:   values** — the horizontal subsampling factor and the vertical subsampling
37:   factor. Default is **2, 2** (chroma subsampled by 2 on both axes). Legal
38:   factors are **1, 2 and 4**
39:   (1 = no subsampling, 2 = half resolution, 4 = quarter resolution along the
40:   axis).
41: - **YCbCrPositioning (531 / 0x0213):** Type SHORT (TIFF data type 3), **1
42:   value**. Default is **1 = centered**. The alternative value is **2 = co-sited**
43:   (chroma sample points aligned with luma sample positions, as used e.g. in
44:   broadcast 4:2:2 workflows).
45: - **ReferenceBlackWhite (532 / 0x0214):** Type RATIONAL (TIFF data type 5), **6
46:   values**. The values are grouped in pairs of (reference black, reference
47:   white) per pixel component, ordered like the components of the
48:   `PhotometricInterpretation = 6` image (Y, Cb, Cr). Default value set:
49:   Y black/white = 0/255, Cb black/white = 128/255, Cr black/white = 128/255.
50: 
51: ## Conversion formulas
52: 
53: ### Forward conversion (RGB -> YCbCr), ITU-R BT.601
54: 
55: - `Y  = 0.299 * R + 0.587 * G + 0.114 * B`
56: - `Cb = -0.168736 * R - 0.331264 * G + 0.5 * B + 128`
57: - `Cr = 0.5 * R - 0.418688 * G - 0.081312 * B + 128`
58: 
59: ### Reverse conversion (YCbCr -> RGB), ITU-R BT.601
60: 
61: - `R = Y + 1.402 * (Cr - 128)`
62: - `G = Y - 0.344136 * (Cb - 128) - 0.714136 * (Cr - 128)`
63: - `B = Y + 1.772 * (Cb - 128)`
64: 
65: ### Reference black/white / headroom and footroom
66: 
67: The `ReferenceBlackWhite` tag supplies, per component, a reference black value
68: and a reference white value. These define the headroom/footroom range of the
69: image data: the black value corresponds to the black end of the coding range and
70: the white value to the white end. The values stored in the image are **codes**;
71: `ReferenceBlackWhite` defines how those codes scale into full-range values when
72: converting to RGB.
73: 
74: For each component the forward scaling is:
75: 
76: `FullRangeValue = (code - ReferenceBlack) * CodingRange / (ReferenceWhite - ReferenceBlack)`
77: 
78: and the reverse scaling is:
79: 
80: `code = (FullRangeValue * (ReferenceWhite - ReferenceBlack) / CodingRange) + ReferenceBlack`
81: 
82: `CodingRange` is the range of full-range values: `2^BitsPerSample - 1` for Y and
83: RGB (255 for 8-bit samples), but **127 for Cb and Cr**. That difference matters:
84: with the default reference values Cb/Cr run from code 128 to code 255, so the
85: chroma scaling reduces to `(code - 128) * 127 / (255 - 128) = code - 128`. This
86: is why the no-headroom case amounts to simply subtracting 128, and why the `128`
87: in `R = Y + 1.402 * (Cr - 128)` is the `ReferenceBlack` value for Cb/Cr in the
88: no-headroom case, not a magic number.
89: 
90: For YCbCr the default reference values are black = 0 and white = 255 for the
91: luma component (Y), and black = 128 and white = 255 for the chroma components
92: (Cb/Cr). Merely subtracting 128 is correct only for these defaults. Images with
93: headroom/footroom carry other reference values: for example, with
94: `ReferenceBlackWhite = [15, 235, 128, 240, 128, 240]` a luma code of 235 maps to
95: `255` and a luma code of 15 maps to `0`, using
96: `(code - 15) * 255 / (235 - 15)`. The chroma white reference is 240 rather than
97: the default 255, so subtracting 128 alone leaves chroma under-scaled. Readers
98: must apply the tag's scaling instead of assuming the defaults.
99: 
100: The TIFF 6.0 specification says the default `ReferenceBlackWhite` values are
101: inappropriate for Class Y images and that the tag must be supplied explicitly.
102: In practice many images omit it, so readers must fall back to the YCbCr-specific
103: defaults above (Y 0/255, Cb/Cr 128/255).
104: 
105: ## Subsampling
106: 
107: - The `YCbCrSubsampling` factors describe how the chroma components are
108:   subsampled relative to the luma component.
109: - Legal subsampling factors are **1, 2 and 4**.
110: - The chroma image dimensions are computed by rounding **up** (ceiling) the
111:   luma dimensions divided by the subsampling factor, so that no chroma sample is
112:   dropped for images whose dimensions are not evenly divisible.
113: - For images using subsampling, strip organization (`RowsPerStrip`) must be
114:   consistent with the luma/chroma grid; `RowsPerStrip` is expressed in luma
115:   rows.
116: 
117: ## Positioning
118: 
119: - `YCbCrPositioning = 1` (default): **centered** positioning of the chroma
120:   samples with respect to the luminance samples.
121: - `YCbCrPositioning = 2`: **co-sited** positioning (chroma sample points aligned
122:   with luma sample points, e.g. recommended for 4:2:2 workflows).
123: 
124: ## Minimum requirements for YCbCr images
125: 
126: In addition to the general Baseline TIFF requirements, a YCbCr file must have:
127: 
128: - `SamplesPerPixel = 3` (Y, Cb, Cr).
129: - `BitsPerSample = 8, 8, 8`.
130: - `Compression = 1` (none), `5` (LZW) or `7` (JPEG; TIFF Technical Note 2).
131: - `PhotometricInterpretation = 6` (YCbCr).
132: - `PlanarConfig = 1` (chunky) or `2` (separate).
133: - `ReferenceBlackWhite`: required by the TIFF 6.0 specification. Readers must
134:   nevertheless handle its absence by falling back to the YCbCr-specific
135:   defaults above (Y 0/255, Cb/Cr 128/255), because many real-world files omit
136:   tag 532.
137: 
138: ## Generating the test images
139: 
140: `tests/ycbcr_images/generate_ycbcr.py` recreates the fixture set. It requires
141: Python 3 and the libtiff and netpbm command-line tools (`pnmtotiff`,
142: `rgb2ycbcr`, `tiffset`, `tiffcp`, `tiff2rgba`, `tifftopnm`). From the repository
143: root, run:
144: 
145: ```sh
146: python3 tests/ycbcr_images/generate_ycbcr.py
147: ```
148: 
149: The pipeline for each fixture is:
150: 
151: 1. Write a deterministic binary P6 source PPM in pure Python (standard-library
152:    `bytes` and `zlib.crc32`; no external imaging library).
153: 2. `pnmtotiff < src.ppm > src.tif` creates an RGB TIFF.
154: 3. `rgb2ycbcr -c none -h H -v V -r HEIGHT src.tif out.tif` writes the YCbCr
155:    image. This writes all four YCbCr tags (529, 530, 531, 532) with the BT.601
156:    coefficients, centered positioning and default reference values.
157: 4. Attributes that `rgb2ycbcr` cannot produce directly are applied with
158:    `tiffset`. RATIONAL tags are set without a count, e.g.
159:    `tiffset -s YCbCrCoefficients 0.2126 0.7152 0.0722 file`. Tiled organization
160:    uses `tiffcp -t -w 16 -l 16 -c none`; because `tiffcp` refuses subsampled
161:    input it tiles a 1x1 image and the four YCbCr tags plus
162:    `PhotometricInterpretation` are restored afterwards.
163: 5. `tiff2rgba -n -c none <tif> <rgba.tif>` followed by
164:    `tifftopnm <rgba.tif> > ycbcr-*.ppm` produces each ground-truth P6 PPM.
165: 
166: The 18 fixtures are described in the matrix below. Six of them (the variants)
167: are tag-reading tests only: `tiffset` changes tag values without reorganizing
168: pixel data. The tiled fixture is additionally limited in that its pixel data is
169: **not** subsampled — the `YCbCrSubsampling` tag is set to `2 2` after tiling —
170: so it is not usable for conversion verification.
171: 
172: ## ImageMagick limitations
173: 
174: ImageMagick is a general-purpose image converter, but its TIFF writer has a
175: fixed set of capabilities that matter for YCbCr coverage:
176: 
177: - It does **not** write `YCbCrCoefficients` (529), `YCbCrSubsampling` (530),
178:   `YCbCrPositioning` (531), or `ReferenceBlackWhite` (532). Requests through
179:   `-define` or `-sampling-factor` do not create those tags; subsampling through
180:   image resizing changes the pixel dimensions instead of writing the tag.
181: - It does **not** support separate planar configuration
182:   (`PlanarConfiguration = 2`).
183: - It can write only basic YCbCr TIFFs: `PhotometricInterpretation = 6`,
184:   `SamplesPerPixel = 3`, 8-bit samples, uncompressed data, and default or absent
185:   YCbCr tags. Tiling is available through
186:   `-define tiff:tile-geometry=<value>`.
187: 
188: These limits are why the fixtures in this repository are generated with
189: libtiff's `rgb2ycbcr` rather than ImageMagick.
190: 
191: ## Test image matrix
192: 
193: All files are in `tests/ycbcr_images/`. The "Kind" column marks a fixture as a
194: **conversion** test (tags and pixel data agree) or a **tag-reading** test.
195: 
196: ### Subsampling fixtures
197: 
198: Nine 64x48 images with default BT.601 coefficients, centered positioning,
199: default reference values, 8-bit contiguous planes and no compression. Each
200: carries a real `YCbCrSubsampling` value written by `rgb2ycbcr`.
201: 
202: | Test image | Subsampling | Kind | Validates |
203: |---|---|---|---|
204: | `ycbcr-1x1.tif` | 1x1 | conversion | Full-resolution YCbCr with all four tags at their defaults; stripped organization. |
205: | `ycbcr-2x1.tif` | 2x1 | conversion | Horizontal-only chroma subsampling. |
206: | `ycbcr-1x2.tif` | 1x2 | conversion | Vertical-only chroma subsampling. |
207: | `ycbcr-2x2.tif` | 2x2 | conversion | Half-resolution chroma on both axes. |
208: | `ycbcr-4x1.tif` | 4x1 | conversion | Quarter-resolution horizontal chroma. |
209: | `ycbcr-1x4.tif` | 1x4 | conversion | Quarter-resolution vertical chroma. |
210: | `ycbcr-4x2.tif` | 4x2 | conversion | Mixed 4x2 chroma grid. |
211: | `ycbcr-2x4.tif` | 2x4 | conversion | Mixed 2x4 chroma grid. |
212: | `ycbcr-4x4.tif` | 4x4 | conversion | Quarter-resolution chroma on both axes. |
213: 
214: ### Variant fixtures
215: 
216: Six 64x48 images with one non-default attribute each. These are tag-reading
217: tests: `tiffset` changes the tag without reorganizing pixel data.
218: 
219: | Test image | Attribute | Kind | Validates |
220: |---|---|---|---|
221: | `ycbcr-cosited.tif` | Positioning = 2 (co-sited) on a 2x2 base | tag-reading | Co-sited chroma positioning. |
222: | `ycbcr-custom-coeffs.tif` | Coefficients = 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722 on a 1x1 base | tag-reading | Non-default luma coefficients (tag 529). |
223: | `ycbcr-custom-refbw.tif` | RefBW = 15/235/128/240/128/240 on a 1x1 base | tag-reading | Headroom/footroom reference values (tag 532). |
224: | `ycbcr-planar-1x1.tif` | PlanarConfig = 2 on a 1x1 base | tag-reading | Separate-plane configuration (tag 284) without subsampling. |
225: | `ycbcr-planar-2x2.tif` | PlanarConfig = 2 on a 2x2 base | tag-reading | Separate-plane configuration (tag 284). |
226: | `ycbcr-tiled-2x2.tif` | 16x16 tiles, 4x3 grid (12 tiles) | tag-reading | Tile tag path together with all four YCbCr tags. |
227: 
228: `ycbcr-tiled-2x2.tif` is a special case: `tiffcp` cannot tile subsampled input,
229: so the image was tiled while still 1x1 and the `YCbCrSubsampling` tag was set to
230: `2 2` afterwards. Its pixel data is therefore not subsampled; the fixture
231: exercises tag reading and tile traversal only.
232: 
233: ### Odd-dimension fixtures
234: 
235: Three images whose width and height are not multiples of the subsampling

243: | `ycbcr-odd-mixed.tif` | 62x47 | 2x1 | conversion | Ceiling on one axis only for mixed subsampling. |
244:

1: # YCbCr (PhotometricInterpretation = 6) Support Reference
2: 
3: This document describes YCbCr (`PhotometricInterpretation = 6`) images as
4: defined by Section 21 of the TIFF 6.0 specification.
5: 
6: ## Scope
7: 
8: - YCbCr image encoding as defined by TIFF 6.0 Section 21.
9: - Conversion between RGB and YCbCr.
10: - Chroma subsampling, positioning, and reference black/white handling.
11: - Minimum requirements for a valid YCbCr TIFF.
12: - Mapping of the test images in `tests/ycbcr_images/` to the specification
13:   topics they exercise.
14: 
15: ## Tag definitions
16: 
17: The following TIFF tags describe the color information of an image whose
18: `PhotometricInterpretation = 6` (YCbCr). They are defined in TIFF 6.0
19: Section 21.
20: 
21: | Tag | Name | TIFF value | Type | Count | Default | Description |
22: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
23: | 529 | YCbCrCoefficients | 0x0211 | RATIONAL (5) / SRATIONAL (10) | 3 | ITU-R BT.601 luma coefficients | Coefficients used for the transformation from RGB to YCbCr. |
24: | 530 | YCbCrSubsampling | 0x0212 | SHORT (3) | 2 | 2, 2 | Horizontal and vertical subsampling factors of the chroma components. |
25: | 531 | YCbCrPositioning | 0x0213 | SHORT (3) | 1 | 1 | Positioning of the chroma samples relative to the luminance samples. |
26: | 532 | ReferenceBlackWhite | 0x0214 | RATIONAL (5) | 6 | (0, 255, 128, 255, 128, 255) | Reference black and white data values (headroom/footroom) per component. |
27: 
28: Notes on the individual tags:
29: 
30: - **YCbCrCoefficients (529 / 0x0211):** Type RATIONAL (TIFF data type 5) or
31:   SRATIONAL (TIFF data type 10), with **3 values** (the RGB -> YCbCr
32:   transformation coefficients, e.g. the luma row). Defaults to the ITU-R BT.601
33:   coefficients (approximately 0.299, 0.587, 0.114 for the red, green and blue
34:   contributions to luma).
35: - **YCbCrSubsampling (530 / 0x0212):** Type SHORT (TIFF data type 3), **2
36:   values** — the horizontal subsampling factor and the vertical subsampling
37:   factor. Default is **2, 2** (chroma subsampled by 2 on both axes). Legal
38:   factors are **1, 2 and 4**
39:   (1 = no subsampling, 2 = half resolution, 4 = quarter resolution along the
40:   axis).
41: - **YCbCrPositioning (531 / 0x0213):** Type SHORT (TIFF data type 3), **1
42:   value**. Default is **1 = centered**. The alternative value is **2 = co-sited**
43:   (chroma sample points aligned with luma sample positions, as used e.g. in
44:   broadcast 4:2:2 workflows).
45: - **ReferenceBlackWhite (532 / 0x0214):** Type RATIONAL (TIFF data type 5), **6
46:   values**. The values are grouped in pairs of (reference black, reference
47:   white) per pixel component, ordered like the components of the
48:   `PhotometricInterpretation = 6` image (Y, Cb, Cr). Default value set:
49:   Y black/white = 0/255, Cb black/white = 128/255, Cr black/white = 128/255.
50: 
51: ## Conversion formulas
52: 
53: ### Forward conversion (RGB -> YCbCr), ITU-R BT.601
54: 
55: - `Y  = 0.299 * R + 0.587 * G + 0.114 * B`
56: - `Cb = -0.168736 * R - 0.331264 * G + 0.5 * B + 128`
57: - `Cr = 0.5 * R - 0.418688 * G - 0.081312 * B + 128`
58: 
59: ### Reverse conversion (YCbCr -> RGB), ITU-R BT.601
60: 
61: - `R = Y + 1.402 * (Cr - 128)`
62: - `G = Y - 0.344136 * (Cb - 128) - 0.714136 * (Cr - 128)`
63: - `B = Y + 1.772 * (Cb - 128)`
64: 
65: ### Reference black/white / headroom and footroom
66: 
67: The `ReferenceBlackWhite` tag supplies, per component, a reference black value
68: and a reference white value. These define the headroom/footroom range of the
69: image data: the black value corresponds to the black end of the coding range and
70: the white value to the white end. The values stored in the image are **codes**;
71: `ReferenceBlackWhite` defines how those codes scale into full-range values when
72: converting to RGB.
73: 
74: For each component the forward scaling is:
75: 
76: `FullRangeValue = (code - ReferenceBlack) * CodingRange / (ReferenceWhite - ReferenceBlack)`
77: 
78: and the reverse scaling is:
79: 
80: `code = (FullRangeValue * (ReferenceWhite - ReferenceBlack) / CodingRange) + ReferenceBlack`
81: 
82: `CodingRange` is the range of full-range values: `2^BitsPerSample - 1` for Y and
83: RGB (255 for 8-bit samples), but **127 for Cb and Cr**. That difference matters:
84: with the default reference values Cb/Cr run from code 128 to code 255, so the
85: chroma scaling reduces to `(code - 128) * 127 / (255 - 128) = code - 128`. This
86: is why the no-headroom case amounts to simply subtracting 128, and why the `128`
87: in `R = Y + 1.402 * (Cr - 128)` is the `ReferenceBlack` value for Cb/Cr in the
88: no-headroom case, not a magic number.
89: 
90: For YCbCr the default reference values are black = 0 and white = 255 for the
91: luma component (Y), and black = 128 and white = 255 for the chroma components
92: (Cb/Cr). Merely subtracting 128 is correct only for these defaults. Images with
93: headroom/footroom carry other reference values: for example, with
94: `ReferenceBlackWhite = [15, 235, 128, 240, 128, 240]` a luma code of 235 maps to
95: `255` and a luma code of 15 maps to `0`, using
96: `(code - 15) * 255 / (235 - 15)`. The chroma white reference is 240 rather than
97: the default 255, so subtracting 128 alone leaves chroma under-scaled. Readers
98: must apply the tag's scaling instead of assuming the defaults.
99: 
100: The TIFF 6.0 specification says the default `ReferenceBlackWhite` values are
101: inappropriate for Class Y images and that the tag must be supplied explicitly.
102: In practice many images omit it, so readers must fall back to the YCbCr-specific
103: defaults above (Y 0/255, Cb/Cr 128/255).
104: 
105: ## Subsampling
106: 
107: - The `YCbCrSubsampling` factors describe how the chroma components are
108:   subsampled relative to the luma component.
109: - Legal subsampling factors are **1, 2 and 4**.
110: - The chroma image dimensions are computed by rounding **up** (ceiling) the
111:   luma dimensions divided by the subsampling factor, so that no chroma sample is
112:   dropped for images whose dimensions are not evenly divisible.
113: - For images using subsampling, strip organization (`RowsPerStrip`) must be
114:   consistent with the luma/chroma grid; `RowsPerStrip` is expressed in luma
115:   rows.
116: 
117: ## Positioning
118: 
119: - `YCbCrPositioning = 1` (default): **centered** positioning of the chroma
120:   samples with respect to the luminance samples.
121: - `YCbCrPositioning = 2`: **co-sited** positioning (chroma sample points aligned
122:   with luma sample points, e.g. recommended for 4:2:2 workflows).
123: 
124: ## Minimum requirements for YCbCr images
125: 
126: In addition to the general Baseline TIFF requirements, a YCbCr file must have:
127: 
128: - `SamplesPerPixel = 3` (Y, Cb, Cr).
129: - `BitsPerSample = 8, 8, 8`.
130: - `Compression = 1` (none), `5` (LZW) or `7` (JPEG; TIFF Technical Note 2).
131: - `PhotometricInterpretation = 6` (YCbCr).
132: - `PlanarConfig = 1` (chunky) or `2` (separate).
133: - `ReferenceBlackWhite`: required by the TIFF 6.0 specification. Readers must
134:   nevertheless handle its absence by falling back to the YCbCr-specific
135:   defaults above (Y 0/255, Cb/Cr 128/255), because many real-world files omit
136:   tag 532.
137: 
138: ## Generating the test images
139: 
140: `tests/ycbcr_images/generate_ycbcr.py` recreates the fixture set. It requires
141: Python 3 and the libtiff and netpbm command-line tools (`pnmtotiff`,
142: `rgb2ycbcr`, `tiffset`, `tiffcp`, `tiff2rgba`, `tifftopnm`). From the repository
143: root, run:
144: 
145: ```sh
146: python3 tests/ycbcr_images/generate_ycbcr.py
147: ```
148: 
149: The pipeline for each fixture is:
150: 
151: 1. Write a deterministic binary P6 source PPM in pure Python (standard-library
152:    `bytes` and `zlib.crc32`; no external imaging library).
153: 2. `pnmtotiff < src.ppm > src.tif` creates an RGB TIFF.
154: 3. `rgb2ycbcr -c none -h H -v V -r HEIGHT src.tif out.tif` writes the YCbCr
155:    image. This writes all four YCbCr tags (529, 530, 531, 532) with the BT.601
156:    coefficients, centered positioning and default reference values.
157: 4. Attributes that `rgb2ycbcr` cannot produce directly are applied with
158:    `tiffset`. RATIONAL tags are set without a count, e.g.
159:    `tiffset -s YCbCrCoefficients 0.2126 0.7152 0.0722 file`. Tiled organization
160:    uses `tiffcp -t -w 16 -l 16 -c none`; because `tiffcp` refuses subsampled
161:    input it tiles a 1x1 image and the four YCbCr tags plus
162:    `PhotometricInterpretation` are restored afterwards.
163: 5. `tiff2rgba -n -c none <tif> <rgba.tif>` followed by
164:    `tifftopnm <rgba.tif> > ycbcr-*.ppm` produces each ground-truth P6 PPM.
165: 
166: The 18 fixtures are described in the matrix below. Six of them (the variants)
167: are tag-reading tests only: `tiffset` changes tag values without reorganizing
168: pixel data. The tiled fixture is additionally limited in that its pixel data is
169: **not** subsampled — the `YCbCrSubsampling` tag is set to `2 2` after tiling —
170: so it is not usable for conversion verification.
171: 
172: ## ImageMagick limitations
173: 
174: ImageMagick is a general-purpose image converter, but its TIFF writer has a
175: fixed set of capabilities that matter for YCbCr coverage:
176: 
177: - It does **not** write `YCbCrCoefficients` (529), `YCbCrSubsampling` (530),
178:   `YCbCrPositioning` (531), or `ReferenceBlackWhite` (532). Requests through
179:   `-define` or `-sampling-factor` do not create those tags; subsampling through
180:   image resizing changes the pixel dimensions instead of writing the tag.
181: - It does **not** support separate planar configuration
182:   (`PlanarConfiguration = 2`).
183: - It can write only basic YCbCr TIFFs: `PhotometricInterpretation = 6`,
184:   `SamplesPerPixel = 3`, 8-bit samples, uncompressed data, and default or absent
185:   YCbCr tags. Tiling is available through
186:   `-define tiff:tile-geometry=<value>`.
187: 
188: These limits are why the fixtures in this repository are generated with
189: libtiff's `rgb2ycbcr` rather than ImageMagick.
190: 
191: ## Test image matrix
192: 
193: All files are in `tests/ycbcr_images/`. The "Kind" column marks a fixture as a
194: **conversion** test (tags and pixel data agree) or a **tag-reading** test.
195: 
196: ### Subsampling fixtures
197: 
198: Nine 64x48 images with default BT.601 coefficients, centered positioning,
199: default reference values, 8-bit contiguous planes and no compression. Each
200: carries a real `YCbCrSubsampling` value written by `rgb2ycbcr`.
201: 
202: | Test image | Subsampling | Kind | Validates |
203: |---|---|---|---|
204: | `ycbcr-1x1.tif` | 1x1 | conversion | Full-resolution YCbCr with all four tags at their defaults; stripped organization. |
205: | `ycbcr-2x1.tif` | 2x1 | conversion | Horizontal-only chroma subsampling. |
206: | `ycbcr-1x2.tif` | 1x2 | conversion | Vertical-only chroma subsampling. |
207: | `ycbcr-2x2.tif` | 2x2 | conversion | Half-resolution chroma on both axes. |
208: | `ycbcr-4x1.tif` | 4x1 | conversion | Quarter-resolution horizontal chroma. |
209: | `ycbcr-1x4.tif` | 1x4 | conversion | Quarter-resolution vertical chroma. |
210: | `ycbcr-4x2.tif` | 4x2 | conversion | Mixed 4x2 chroma grid. |
211: | `ycbcr-2x4.tif` | 2x4 | conversion | Mixed 2x4 chroma grid. |
212: | `ycbcr-4x4.tif` | 4x4 | conversion | Quarter-resolution chroma on both axes. |
213: 
214: ### Variant fixtures
215: 
216: Six 64x48 images with one non-default attribute each. These are tag-reading

218: 
219: | Test image | Attribute | Kind | Validates |
220: |---|---|---|---|
221: | `ycbcr-cosited.tif` | Positioning = 2 (co-sited) on a 2x2 base | tag-reading | Co-sited chroma positioning. |
222: | `ycbcr-custom-coeffs.tif` | Coefficients = 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722 on a 1x1 base | tag-reading | Non-default luma coefficients (tag 529). |
223: | `ycbcr-custom-refbw.tif` | RefBW = 15/235/128/240/128/240 on a 1x1 base | tag-reading | Headroom/footroom reference values (tag 532). |
224: | `ycbcr-planar-1x1.tif` | PlanarConfig = 2 on a 1x1 base | tag-reading | Separate-plane configuration (tag 284) without subsampling. |
225: | `ycbcr-planar-2x2.tif` | PlanarConfig = 2 on a 2x2 base | tag-reading | Separate-plane configuration (tag 284). |
226: | `ycbcr-tiled-2x2.tif` | 16x16 tiles, 4x3 grid (12 tiles) | tag-reading | Tile tag path together with all four YCbCr tags. |
227:

26:   ReferenceBlack. Headroom/footroom example

28:   chroma white 240 vs default 255). Spec note: RefBW is required by TIFF 6.0
29:   but inappropriate for Class Y defaults; readers must fall back to
